newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina insists no extradition for Blond Angel.
newsitem.headline: Argentina insists no extradition for Blond Angel.

text.p: Argentina has insisted it will not extradite a navy captain wanted in France for the murder of two French nuns in the "Dirty War" of the late 1970s despite a plea from French President Jacques Chirac.

Argentine Justice Minister Elias Jassan said in comments reported by the local media on Thursday that he sympathises with Chirac's wish that Capt. Alfredo Astiz, known as "the Blond Angel," serve time in a French jail for the murders.

France has an international arrest warrant out for Astiz, who retired in 1996 after years of pressure from human rights groups. He has been sentenced to life in jail in absentia by French courts for the murder of nuns Alice Dumon and Leonie Duquet.
Argentina declared an amnesty in 1989 for all human rights crimes of the brutal 1976-83 military regime, when tens of thousands of people died or disappeared.

Under Argentine law, Astiz cannot be extradited for crimes "that for our country are a closed case," Jassan said. "Laws exist which we have to respect and in that sense the Astiz issue is a closed case for our country. That is the reality, like it or not."

Chirac told reporters in Buenos Aires on Tuesday, the last day of a Latin American tour, that it was his "wish that the murderer serve his sentence in France. I respect Argentine law but I am very sorry that he has not been punished."

Astiz is also wanted by Sweden for the disappearance of Swedish student Dagmar Hagelin the same year as the nuns. Like them, she is believed to have been taken to the most infamous torture centre of the Dirty War, the Navy School of Mechanics.
